plan.title: AppSec: 2 HIGH + 1 MEDIUM — post-#3336 UAT Shell residuals (nc/7zz/msgfmt… plant authz grants + kill-switch) + slices.jsonl leaf diversion

narratives.Description: Post-#3336 UAT Shell still classifies residual write-capable binaries as empty or unclassifiable and allows write-shaped commands. Those residuals can plant forged .deft/authz grants or a regular-file .deft-directive-disable kill-switch. Separately, slices.jsonl append still uses a raw writer and follows an in-tree leaf symlink.
narratives.UserStory: As a Directive operator under active UAT, I want residual write-capable Shell bins and the slices.jsonl writer to stay fail-closed, so that agents cannot plant authz grants, plant a kill-switch, or divert slice appends into tracked files.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: Extended classify residual-bin detection and dest-flag parsing. Routed slice record appends through containedWrite. Added AppSec regressions and CHANGELOG note.
narratives.Overview: Shipped in PR 3359. Residual UAT Shell writers deny authz and kill-switch plants; slices.jsonl append uses containedWrite.

items.title: UAT residual bins deny authz and kill-switch writes

narrative.Acceptance: Given active UAT, when listed residual bins (nc, netcat, 7zz, msgfmt, msgcat, lz4, lzop, unrar, rar, aunpack, atool, ftpget, tftp, sqlite3, crane, objcopy) write into .deft/authz or plant .deft-directive-disable / .no-deft-directive, they classify as settings deny. Dest-flag parsing covers -o / --output / --outfile and bin-specific dest forms including 7zz attached -oDIR. Unclassifiable write-shaped Shell under UAT is fail-closed, not silent allow. Ordinary non-authz dests such as /tmp stay allowed outside UAT write paths. Regression tests cover residual bins versus already-denied ncat / 7z / msguniq peers.

x-directive/evidence.pointer: packages/core/src/authz/incident-regression.test.ts denies residual writer authz/kill-switch plant under UAT (#3354); PR https://github.com/deftai/directive/pull/3359

narrative.Acceptance: Given writeSliceUnlocked or slice:record-existing, when xbrief/.triage-cache/slices.jsonl is an in-tree leaf symlink or an out-of-containment destination, the write is refused via containedWrite or assertWriteTargetSafe. An AppSec regression plants a leaf symlink to a tracked fixture and asserts the append does not divert and the fixture stays intact.

x-directive/evidence.pointer: packages/core/src/slice/record.test.ts leaf-symlink + out-of-containment; existing.test.ts record-existing refuse; PR https://github.com/deftai/directive/pull/3359

narrative.Acceptance: Given the security fix lands, when CHANGELOG [Unreleased] is read, it has a brief security note for #3354 with no exploit cookbook.

acceptance.derived_reason: derived 12 independently testable clauses from the task statement before product edit (#3323)

clauses.text: Under active UAT, listed residual binaries that write into `.deft/authz/` classify as settings deny (not unclassifiable allow)
Same bins targeting `.deft-directive-disable` / `.no-deft-directive` classify as settings deny
Dest-flag parsing covers `-o` / `--output` / `--outfile` / bin-specific dest forms (including 7zz attached `-oDIR` if that is the dest form)
Prefer fail-closed on unclassifiable write-shaped Shell under UAT (not silent allow). Do not stop at named-peer allowlists.
Regression tests cover residual bins vs already-denied peers (`ncat` / `7z` / `msguniq`)
No false deny of ordinary non-authz / non-kill-switch dests (e.g. `/tmp`) outside UAT write paths
*MEDIUM — slices.jsonl writer (same PR preferred; may split if needed)

`writeSliceUnlocked` / `slice:record-existing` refuse leaf symlinks / out-of-containment destinations (`containedWrite` / `assertWriteTargetSafe` parity with candidates / summary / reconcile / bootstrap)
AppSec regression: leaf symlink → in-tree target does not divert the append; tracked fixture stays intact
CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` security note (brief; no exploit cookbook)
